verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is published wire copy. The -10%/-12% FY26 revenue guide was issued with the Q3 release on 2026-05-07 and carried by Businesswire, Seeking Alpha and MSN the same day; the nine-month revenue and the Q4 FY25 base are in the same 8-K exhibit the hunter cites; and the $1.50bn full-year consensus is published on public estimate pages. The 'finding' is one subtraction on two public numbers, and it lands exactly where you would expect: $1.50bn is simply the midpoint of the company's own guide ($1.484-1.517bn), so 'consensus implies a step-down versus run-rate' is the generic arithmetic property of any guided-midpoint consensus, not a discovery about FLWS. The premise is also weaker than stated: -11.1%, -9.5%, -11.6% is not a 'remarkably steady rate', it is a re-acceleration, and Q4 (Apr-Jun) is the Mother's Day quarter where the Consumer Floral segment that fell 18.7% in Q3 carries the heaviest mix weight — which is a reason the favourable end of the guide is the less likely end, not the more likely one. Finally the mechanism is thin for this name: the last two prints moved +16.5% and +14.6% on a large revenue miss with a $45.2m impairment and on holiday-quarter results, so a $10m revenue delta against a $228m market cap is not what sets the tape here.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q3 FY26 revenue $293.0m (-11.6%), and FY26 guidance of revenue down approximately 10%-12% with adjusted EBITDA about break-even +/-$2m.
Wire-level coverage of the same -10%/-12% revenue and break-even EBITDA guide the finding's arithmetic is built on.
Publishes the FY2026 consensus revenue forecast as unchanged at US$1.50bn, the second number the finding's arithmetic uses.
The 8-K exhibit containing nine-month revenue of $1,210.4m (-10.3%) and the prior-year quarterly bases.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Reaction history argues against revenue being the driver: +16.54% on 2026-05-07 came alongside an 11.6% revenue decline and a $45.2m impairment, and +14.60% on 2026-01-29. A name that rallies 16% on a revenue miss is not being traded off a $10m Q4 revenue delta. Run-up of -11.88% over 20 days into the print is consistent with the market already discounting the weaker end of the guide.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A published Q4-specific revenue estimate materially below $290m, or evidence that the sell-side models Q4 at the guide low end rather than the midpoint, would make the run-rate extrapolation a genuine variant view rather than a restatement of the guide.
verdicts.notes: Arithmetic verified: nine-month FY25 implied ~$1,349m, FY25 total ~$1,686m, -10%/-12% gives $1,517m/$1,484m, less $1,210.4m gives $306.6m/$273.6m. The hunter's numbers check out; it is the novelty and the inference that do not.

verdicts.strongest_argument: 'FLWS is a heavily shorted squeeze candidate' is one of the most widely republished facts about this ticker. Fintel, shortsqueeze.com, Benzinga and MarketBeat all carry dedicated FLWS short-interest and short-squeeze-score pages, FINRA publishes the underlying number twice a month, and the stock has already been swept into a meme-stock rally on exactly this basis. Two of the last three prints produced +16.5% and +14.6% one-day moves — the squeeze-on-print dynamic is not a hypothesis, it is the observed reaction history sitting in the sealed baseline. Worse, three of the four numbers in the finding's second clause (6,544 total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM spread 67% of mid) are copied verbatim from the sealed baseline's own options block, so they are by construction not new information, and the low average volume (199,621) is likewise a sealed-baseline field. The one genuinely new-looking claim is the 4.33 -> 48.96 days-to-cover jump, and it does not survive its own source: the MarketBeat series the hunter cites reads 25.88 (3/13), 33.04 (4/15), 4.33 (4/30), 7.52 (5/15), 22.75 (6/15), 36.35 (7/15), 30.67 (7/31), 48.96 (8/14). 4.33 is the single lowest reading in the series, chosen as the base. And 'the short base has not moved all year' is contradicted on the same page: shares short fell from 9,299,354 (3/13) to 7,754,157 (8/14), a 17% reduction — shorts have been covering steadily, not standing still.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the full 2026 settlement-date series including 7,754,157 shares (25.3% of float, 48.96 days to cover) on 8/14 and 9,299,354 shares (30.3%) on 3/13 — the same page shows both the finding's numbers and the decline it denies.
Maintains a standing FLWS short-squeeze page with short interest, float percentage, borrow rates and a short-squeeze score.
Dedicated FLWS short-squeeze page tracking short interest and squeeze conditions.
Exchange-published semi-monthly short interest and days-to-cover for FLWS.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Directly in the baseline: avg_volume_20d 199,621, total_open_interest 6,544, put_call_open_interest_ratio 0.61, atm_spread_frac_of_mid 0.667 are the finding's own figures. Reaction history median absolute move 11.49% with +16.54% and +14.60% on the two most recent up-prints shows the squeeze mechanism has already fired twice and is embedded in what the market expects from this event. The option chain itself says nothing usable (9 days to expiry, 6,544 contracts, 67%-of-mid spread) and I do not lean on it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that borrow cost or utilisation has stepped up sharply since 14 August, or a September FINRA settlement showing the short base re-building rather than continuing to shrink, would make the constraint newly binding rather than a re-telling of a two-year-old story.
verdicts.notes: The finding's central factual assertion ('has not moved all year') is refuted by its own cited source.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this are public documents that anyone covering the name has read. The 2025-09-04 press release — a Businesswire item and an 8-K exhibit — is where the 'pivotal period of foundation setting' framing and the absence of numerical FY26 guidance appear, and I confirmed by fetching it that it gives strategic priorities and no numbers. The May 2026 call, at which management gave no FY27 figures and flagged the $12-13m of consultant costs rolling off 30 June, is published in full transcript on Motley Fool, Investing.com and The Globe and Mail. So the observation is: a company that did not guide last September and did not guide in May is unlikely to guide this September. That is the default expectation, not a variant one. Crucially, the outcome of the exact event this finding describes is already in the sealed baseline: the 2025-09-04 no-guidance print moved the stock -2.81%, comfortably inside the 5.75% deadband. The market has seen this movie and priced it as a non-event. The finding also has no clean sign — absence of a FY27 guide can read as persistent uncertainty (negative) or as removing a disappointing number from the tape (positive) — and a finding whose direction is ambiguous cannot carry much of a ranking.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The FY25 fourth-quarter release describes FY2026 as a foundation-building period with strategic priorities and provides no numerical FY2026 guidance — confirmed by direct fetch.
Full public transcript of the May 2026 call, including the FY26-only guide and the consultant/incentive cost commentary, with no FY27 numbers.
The Q3 release guides FY26 only and quantifies the ~$22m of incentive compensation and consultant costs inside the fiscal year.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline's own history contains the resolution of the identical setup: 2025-09-04, bmo, -2.81%, inside the 5.75% deadband. That is the market's revealed pricing of a no-guidance September print at this company. The other three prints since then (+3.72%, +14.60%, +16.54%) all cleared the deadband on quarter content, not on guidance.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A concrete reason to expect a break in behaviour tomorrow — a stated intention to reinstate guidance, an investor-day announcement, or a change of CFO/CEO messaging since May — would turn a base rate into an event.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The Second Amendment has been on the tape since 2025-05-07 in an 8-K, and has been restated in the FY25 10-K filed 2025-09-05 and in each of the three FY26 10-Qs, most recently the Q3 10-Q filed 2026-05-07 which states the company was in compliance with the minimum-liquidity covenant as of 29 March 2026 with $50.7m of cash and $94.3m of net debt. This is a primary document that every analyst on a 3-analyst small cap has read four times. More damagingly, the 8-K itself undercuts the risk the finding implies: the same amendment that installed the liquidity covenant also *decreased* the minimum fixed-charge coverage ratio and *increased* the maximum leverage ratio for the period running through the fiscal quarter ending 28 March 2027. So what snaps back on 27 December 2026 is not the original ratio test but a deliberately loosened one — the amendment was engineered as a glide path, not a cliff, and the finding presents it as the latter. The revolver step-down to $125m (or $50m in the Affected Period) between 1 January and 1 July is likewise a seasonal facility sizing disclosed sixteen months ago and already lived through once in FY26 without incident. The residual live question — whether the FY26 10-K's going-concern look-forward window, which now spans the snapback, carries new language — is real, but it was equally true of last year's 10-K (whose window ran past September 2026) and produced nothing.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Discloses the Second Amendment: minimum-liquidity covenant until the quarter ending 27 December 2026, revolver cut to $205m with seasonal reduction to $125m / $50m from 1 January to 1 July, and a decreased minimum fixed-charge coverage ratio and increased maximum leverage ratio through the quarter ending 28 March 2027.
The FY2025 10-K restates the amended covenant structure, the revolver commitment reduction and the compliance position.
Q3 FY26 10-Q coverage noting compliance with the minimum-liquidity covenant as of 29 March 2026, $50.7m cash, $94.3m net debt, and expected sufficient liquidity through fiscal 2026.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Run-up of -11.88% over 20 days and a spot 36.99% below the 52-week high are consistent with a market already discounting balance-sheet and turnaround stress rather than being blind to it. The option chain offers nothing usable on downside pricing here — total open interest 6,544, ATM spread 67% of mid, skew_25d null — so I make no claim from it. Timing note: the FY25 10-K landed one day after the FY25 release (04 Sep -> 05 Sep 2025), so the FY26 10-K plausibly lands 10-11 September and can reach the measured move, but the print-day reaction is set by the release and the 8:00 ET call, not by a risk-factor paragraph filed afterwards.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Concede substantially if the finding had shown the specific minimum-liquidity dollar threshold against a projected FY27 seasonal trough, or evidence that projected FY27 EBITDA fails the loosened fixed-charge test at 28 March 2027 — a quantified breach path, rather than the existence of a snapback date, would be genuinely unpriced.

interactions: Three real overlaps. (1) FLWS-h1#1's second clause is not independent evidence at all: '6,544 contracts total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM bid-ask 67% of mid' are verbatim the sealed baseline's options block (total_open_interest 6544, put_call_open_interest_ratio 0.61, atm_spread_frac_of_mid 0.667), and the ~200k/day average volume is the baseline's avg_volume_20d of 199,621. The hunter has re-reported the baseline it was given as a finding; those components should carry no incremental weight. (2) FLWS-h1#2 and the baseline history rest on the same event: the finding's premise is the 2025-09-04 no-guidance print, and that print's realised -2.81% reaction is row four of the baseline's history block, so the finding and its own resolution are the same document — it cannot be scored as though the market has not seen the outcome. (3) FLWS-h1#0 and FLWS-h1#2 are in tension on mechanism: #0 assumes the FY26 guide is the frame the market prices Q4 against, while #2 argues management gives no forward numbers, which means a Q4 revenue beat at the favourable end must carry the entire move with no FY27 anchor beside it. If #2 is right about tomorrow, #0's channel is narrower than stated. Separately, FLWS-h1#0 and FLWS-h1#2 both draw on the FY26 guidance language in the 2026-05-07 release/call, but on different sentences, so that is shared source rather than double-counted fact. FLWS-h1#3 stands on its own document set.
